JsonWebKey.description:
Tagged union of public parameters for all supported JWK key types.
The `kty` field in the serialized form determines which variant is used.

RsaPublicParameters.description: Public parameters for an RSA key (modulus `n` and exponent `e`).

EcPublicParameters.description:
Public parameters for an Elliptic Curve key, consisting of the
curve identifier and the affine coordinates (`x`, `y`).

crv.description: The named curve this key belongs to

x.description: X coordinate of the public point

y.description: Y coordinate of the public point

Public parameters for an Octet Key Pair (OKP) key, such as
Ed25519 or X25519.

listeners.description: Ordered list of listeners to start

trusted_proxies.description: CIDR ranges of reverse proxies trusted to set `X-Forwarded-For`

public_base_url.description: Externally reachable base URL of the authentication service

issuer.description: OIDC issuer identifier. Falls back to `public_base_url` when omitted.

max_body_bytes.description:
Maximum accepted request-body size, in bytes. Requests exceeding this
limit are rejected with `413 Payload Too Large` before they reach a
handler. Defaults to 1 MiB to match the Arkret
`ak.server.read.describe.limits.max_body_bytes` advertisement.

request_timeout_seconds.description:
Per-request handling deadline, in seconds. Long-running upstream calls
have their own timeouts; this guards against accidentally unbounded
handlers. Defaults to 30 seconds. Set to 0 to disable.

shutdown_grace_seconds.description:
Grace period (seconds) granted to in-flight requests when the process
receives SIGTERM/SIGINT before the listener is forcibly closed.
Defaults to 30 seconds.

hsts.description:
Browser HTTP Strict-Transport-Security policy. Disabled by default
because TLS frequently terminates upstream and HSTS has cache
semantics that can lock operators out of an HTTP-only host if
emitted by mistake. Opt in only when this process or the trusted
edge serves HTTPS to end users.

csp_html.description:
`Content-Security-Policy` value emitted on every HTML response.
JSON / asset responses are unaffected. Set to an empty string to
suppress the header entirely (for example, when a downstream CDN
injects its own policy). When omitted, a conservative default
scoped to `'self'` is applied — no third-party scripts, no
inline scripts, no framing. Tighten or relax via this field.
csp_html.default: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'

ArkretConfig.description:
Arkret-specific deployment settings layered on top of the generic OIDC
and account-management configuration.

stations.description:
Station audiences trusted to consume session grants and admin
tokens emitted by coauth.

owning_station.description:
Name of the Station that owns this deployment-private Account
Authority component. A single configured Station is selected
automatically; deployments with multiple Station trust edges must set
this explicitly.

deployment_profile.description:
Deployment profile that gates principal DID method choices.

`did:web` is only valid for principal DIDs when this is
`personal_node` and `principal_method` is explicitly `did:web`.
Other built-in profiles use `did:webvh` for coauth-managed
principal issuance.

principal_method.description:
Principal DID method selected by this deployment.

Defaults to `did:webvh`; setting `did:web` is accepted only for
`deployment_profile=personal_node`.

identity_registry.description:
External DID / identity registry resolver used for Arkret identity
binding workflows.

session_grant_ttl.description:
Lifetime of Arkret session grants, in seconds.

These are the DPoP-bound JWT grants returned by the REST auth bridge
login/exchange paths and rotated through
`/_arkret/gate/account/session-grants/refresh`. Default: 28800 (8h) —
access bearers minted from a grant are short-lived (capped Station
side), so a multi-hour grant gives a normal working session without
long-lived bearers, within the spec ceiling (minutes-to-hours).

admin_audience.description:
Audience string expected by Arkret admin integrations.

Session-grant audiences are `did_core_id` values (the target service's
stable authorization identity). When omitted, the backend falls back to
this deployment's own runtime service core id.

high_risk_threshold.description:
Minimum number of distinct admin DID approvals required to execute a
high-risk risk-action proposal. Defaults to `2`.

"High-risk" actions today are `disable`, `erase`, and `reset_recovery`;
the action `lock` is treated as low-risk and only needs the proposer's
own approval.

trust_domain.description:
Round R2/R3 (2026-05-20) — deployment trust-domain identifier
injected into Realm policy and the server-describe document.

Wire form: `ak:trust_domain:<scope>` where `<scope>` matches
`[a-z0-9._:-]{1,128}`. This value binds peer and recovery
authorization transcripts to the deployment.

When omitted, callers expected to honour cross-deployment replay
protection (`Realm` policy, station describe) MUST be
told the trust domain is unset and fail closed.

Typically provisioned consistently across the deployment.

password_login_session_grants_enabled.description:
Fail-closed gate for the temporary password-login bridge that returns a
Arkret station session grant directly from
`POST /_coauth/gate/account/auth/login`.

Defaults to `false`: production callers must use the OIDC/passkey bridge
and proof-bound grant exchange. When enabled for development, the login
handler still requires a valid DPoP proof before minting the grant.

admin_org_id.description:
Deployment-scoped organization id accepted by the Admin API.

coauth does not yet model true multi-tenant ownership on every entity.
Setting this makes admin requests supply the same
`x-coauth-org-id` value and rejects all other orgs, so a deployment can
fail closed instead of pretending cross-tenant admin isolation exists.

audit_signature_fail_closed.description:
Require signed admin-audit writes to succeed before committing
security-sensitive admin mutations. Defaults to `false` so existing
deployments tolerate missing service signing keys during rollout; set
to `true` in production once JWKS publication and key rotation are
operational.

erasure_request_max_auth_age.description:
Fresh high-risk-action authentication ceiling, in seconds, for the
self-service erasure entry point
`ak.gate.account.command.request_erasure.v1`
(`POST /_arkret/gate/account/erasure-requests`).

account-lifecycle.md §8.1 makes the Account Authority judge
authentication freshness locally from its own facts (recent login,
WebAuthn, recovery key). This value is that deployment policy: the
caller's most recent local authentication must be at most this many
seconds old. When omitted the deployment has no fresh high-risk
authentication policy, so every erasure request fails closed with
`reauthentication_required` and zero writes.

development_auto_enrollment_hosts.description:
Exact local HTTPS host names eligible for development-mode automatic
station trust enrollment.

Every entry must be a bare lowercase host name (no scheme, port, path
or wildcard). Auto-enrollment only runs when ALL of these hold: the
process runs in explicit development mode, the configured endpoint is
an HTTPS URL whose host exactly matches one entry, and neither a
config pin nor a persisted enrollment exists. It never overwrites an
existing pin and must stay empty in production.

StationConfig.description: Trusted Station metadata published through Arkret discovery.

name.description: Human-readable identifier for the consumer, such as `soland-prod`.

endpoint.description: Base URL of the Station integration point.

service_id.description:
Stable service identity core for authenticated S2S authorization.

Optional explicit authorization pin, highest priority. When omitted,
the effective pin comes from the persisted trust enrollment written by
`coauth station trust bootstrap` (or, under the strict
development-mode gate, the automatic first enrollment). Describe
metadata may confirm a pin but can never discover or replace it; an
endpoint URL or bearer token is never converted into an identity core.
A configured value that conflicts with the persisted enrollment fails
startup closed.

session_grant_introspection_bearer.description:
Optional static bearer for the Account Authority / Station
trust edge. The Station presents it to coauth introspection and
Auth-side logout; coauth presents the same deployment credential when
reading the standard agent projection for lifecycle authorization.

embedded_webvh_registration_bearer.description:
Optional static bearer token coauth should send when writing embedded
`did:webvh` registration records into this Station.

Aggregates all cryptographic material: signing keys, encryption keys,
and optional key directories

Hex-encoded encryption key for secure cookies (64 hex characters = 32
bytes).

The key ID (`kid`) as used in JWK headers.

minimum_complexity.description:
Minimum zxcvbn complexity score (0-4):
  0 = <100 guesses, 1 = <10k, 2 = <1M, 3 = <100M, 4 = beyond

HashingScheme.description: A versioned set of parameters that controls how passwords are hashed

version.description: Monotonic version tag -- the highest version is used for new passwords

unicode_normalization.description:
Apply NFKC normalization before hashing. Normally `false`; enable only
when importing hashes that were produced with that normalization step.

secret.description:
Pepper secret mixed into the hash -- makes brute-force harder after a

secret_file.description: Like `secret` but read from an external file

PolicyConfig.description:
Policy engine configuration.

Currently the only supported backend is Cedar.

engine.description:
The policy engine to use.

Defaults to `cedar`.

cedar_policy_file.description:
Path to the Cedar policy file (used when engine is `cedar`).

The file should contain Cedar policy statements.

audit_logging.description:
Whether to enable audit logging for policy evaluations.

When enabled, every policy evaluation will be logged with the action
type, result (violation count or error), and evaluation duration.

PolicyEngine.description: The policy engine backend to use for policy evaluation.

Amazon Cedar policy backend.

Uses Cedar policies evaluated natively in Rust.
Requires the `cedar` feature to be enabled.

registration.description:
Controls how many registrations attempts are permitted
based on source address.

directory_lookup.description:
Directory lookup rate limits. Applies to public handle resolution
surfaces that can otherwise be abused for account enumeration.

identity_resolution.description:
Public identity-resolution read limits. Applies to the DID resolve and
pinned-document read surfaces.

did_binding.description:
DID-binding rate limits. Applies to admin-driven attach/remove
of principal DIDs on accounts.

per_ip.description:
Controls how many account recovery attempts are permitted
based on source IP address.
This can protect against causing e-mail spam to many targets.

Note: this limit also applies to re-sends.

per_address.description:
Controls how many account recovery attempts are permitted
based on the e-mail address entered into the recovery form.
This can protect against causing e-mail spam to one target.

Note: this limit also applies to re-sends.

RateLimiterConfiguration.description:
Configuration for a single rate limiter, specifying burst allowance and
replenishment rate.

burst.description:
A one-off burst of actions that the user can perform
in one go without waiting.

per_second.description:
How quickly the allowance replenishes, in number of actions per second.
Can be fractional to replenish slower.

per_ip.description:
Controls how many login attempts are permitted
based on source IP address.
This can protect against brute force login attempts.

Note: this limit also applies to password checks when a user attempts to
change their own password.

per_account.description:
Controls how many login attempts are permitted
based on the account that is being attempted to be logged into.
This can protect against a distributed brute force attack
but should be set high enough to prevent someone's account being
casually locked out.

Note: this limit also applies to password checks when a user attempts to
change their own password.

lockout.description: Temporary lockout after consecutive failed password logins.

LoginLockoutConfig.description:
Failed-login lockout for password authentication.

This is not the same control as the sliding-window limiters above and does
not subsume them: a limiter throttles *attempt rate* and spends its
allowance on successful logins too, so a patient attacker who stays under
the rate keeps guessing forever. A lockout counts *consecutive failures*
against one account and stops the guessing outright until the window
elapses or a correct password resets the counter.

consecutive_failures.description:
Consecutive failed password attempts that lock the account. `0`
disables the lockout.

lockout_seconds.description: How long the account stays locked once the threshold is reached.

failure_window_seconds.description:
How long a failure counts toward the consecutive total. A failure older
than this is forgotten, so occasional typos spread over days never
accumulate into a lockout.

per_ip.description:
Controls how many email authentication attempts are permitted
based on the source IP address.
This can protect against causing e-mail spam to many targets.

per_address.description:
Controls how many email authentication attempts are permitted
based on the e-mail address entered into the authentication form.
This can protect against causing e-mail spam to one target.

Note: this limit also applies to re-sends.

emails_per_session.description:
Controls how many authentication emails are permitted to be sent per
authentication session. This ensures not too many authentication codes
are created for the same authentication session.

attempt_per_session.description:
Controls how many code authentication attempts are permitted per
authentication session. This can protect against brute-forcing the
code.

per_ip.description:
Controls how many phone authentication attempts are permitted
based on the source IP address.
This can protect against causing SMS spam to many targets.

per_phone.description:
Controls how many phone authentication attempts are permitted
based on the phone number entered into the authentication form.
This can protect against causing SMS spam to one target.

Note: this limit also applies to re-sends.

sms_per_session.description:
Controls how many authentication SMS messages are permitted to be sent
per authentication session. This ensures not too many verification
codes are created for the same phone authentication session.

attempt_per_session.description:
Controls how many code authentication attempts are permitted per
authentication session. This can protect against brute-forcing the
code.

per_ip.description:
Controls how many directory handle lookups are permitted from a
single source IP over the sliding window.

Controls how many public identity reads are permitted from one source
IP over the sliding window.

Controls how many DID-binding mutations are permitted from a
single source IP. Tuned conservatively — admin tooling is the
expected caller, not end-user traffic.

per_account.description:
Controls how many DID-binding mutations are permitted against a
single target account, regardless of source.

UpstreamOAuthConfig.description: Holds the list of upstream OAuth identity providers

Whether this provider is enabled.

Defaults to `true`

issuer.description:
The OIDC issuer URL

This is required if OIDC discovery is enabled (which is the default)

human_name.description: A human-readable name for the provider, that will be shown to users

A brand identifier used to customise the UI, e.g. `apple`, `google`,
`github`, etc.

Values supported by the default template are:

 - `apple`
 - `google`
 - `facebook`
 - `github`
 - `gitlab`
 - `twitter`
 - `discord`
 - `qq`
 - `feishu`
 - `lark`
 - `dingtalk`
 - `wechat`
 - `wecom`

client_id.description: The client ID to use when authenticating with the provider

client_secret_file.description:
Path to the file containing the client secret. The client secret is used
by the `client_secret_basic`, `client_secret_post` and
`client_secret_jwt` authentication methods.

client_secret.description:
Alternative to `client_secret_file`: Reads the client secret directly
from the config.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: The method to authenticate the client with the provider

token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg.description:
The JWS algorithm to use when authenticating the client with the
provider

Used by the `client_secret_jwt` and `private_key_jwt` methods

id_token_signed_response_alg.description:
Expected signature for the JWT payload returned by the token
authentication endpoint.

Defaults to `RS256`.

scope.description:
The scopes to request from the provider

Defaults to `openid`.

discovery_mode.description:
How to discover the provider's configuration

Defaults to `oidc`, which uses OIDC discovery with strict metadata
verification

pkce_method.description:
Whether to use proof key for code exchange (PKCE) when requesting and
exchanging the token.

Defaults to `auto`, which uses PKCE if the provider supports it.

fetch_userinfo.description:
Whether to fetch the user profile from the userinfo endpoint,
or to rely on the data returned in the `id_token` from the
`token_endpoint`.

Defaults to `false`.

userinfo_signed_response_alg.description:
Expected signature for the JWT payload returned by the userinfo
endpoint.

If not specified, the response is expected to be an unsigned JSON
payload.

authorization_endpoint.description:
The URL to use for the provider's authorization endpoint

Defaults to the `authorization_endpoint` provided through discovery

userinfo_endpoint.description:
The URL to use for the provider's userinfo endpoint

Defaults to the `userinfo_endpoint` provided through discovery

token_endpoint.description:
The URL to use for the provider's token endpoint

Defaults to the `token_endpoint` provided through discovery

jwks_uri.description:
The URL to use for getting the provider's public keys

Defaults to the `jwks_uri` provided through discovery

response_mode.description: The response mode we ask the provider to use for the callback

claims_imports.description:
How claims should be imported from the `id_token` provided by the
provider

additional_authorization_parameters.description:
Additional parameters to include in the authorization request

Orders of the keys are not preserved.

forward_login_hint.description:
Whether the `login_hint` should be forwarded to the provider in the
authorization request.

Defaults to `false`.

Use OIDC discovery with relaxed metadata verification

ClaimsImports.description: Governs how user attributes are imported from the upstream provider

subject.description: How to determine the subject of the user

skip_confirmation.description:
When `true`, the interactive confirmation screen is skipped.
Requires `handle.action` to be `require` and other attribute
actions to be `ignore`, `force`, or `require`.

displayname.description: Import the displayname of the user

email.description: Import the email address of the user

avatar.description: Import the avatar URL of the user

account_name.description: Set a human-readable name for the upstream account for display purposes

HandleImportPreference.description: Controls how the local account handle is imported from upstream claims.

on_conflict.description: How to handle conflicts on the handle claim

ImportAction.description: Controls how a single upstream claim is handled during account linking

oneOf.description: Pre-fill the claim value but let the user modify it

Overwrite the local value unconditionally (fail if missing)

OnConflict.description:
Determines what happens when an upstream identity matches an existing
local account

oneOf.description: Reject the upstream login when a conflict is detected
Link the upstream identity unconditionally, even if another link exists

Link only when no prior link for this provider exists on the user

Log out all sessions started by this OIDC session, including coauth

BrandingConfig.description: Configuration section for tweaking the branding of the service

service_name.description: A human-readable name. Defaults to the server's address.

policy_uri.description:
Link to a privacy policy, displayed in the footer of web pages and
emails. It is also advertised to clients through the `op_policy_uri`
OIDC provider metadata.

tos_uri.description:
Link to a terms of service document, displayed in the footer of web
pages and emails. It is also advertised to clients through the
`op_tos_uri` OIDC provider metadata.

imprint.description:
Legal imprint, displayed in the footer in the footer of web pages and
emails.

logo_uri.description: Logo displayed in some web pages.

CaptchaConfig.description: Controls CAPTCHA-based bot protection for sensitive operations

service.description: The CAPTCHA provider to use, if any

site_key.description: Public-facing site key provided by the CAPTCHA service

secret_key.description: Server-side secret key for verifying CAPTCHA responses

AccountConfig.description: Knobs for user-facing account management features

email_change_allowed.description: Whether users can update their own email address (default: `true`)

displayname_change_allowed.description:
Whether users can update their display name (default: `true`).
Keep in sync with the downstream principal policy.

password_registration_enabled.description:
Enable self-service password-based registration (default: `false`).
Ignored when password login is disabled entirely.

password_registration_contact_required.description:
Require at least one verified contact method for password-based
registrations (default: `true`). Has no effect when registration is off.

registration_email_delivery_bypass_allow.description:
Allow registration strands to bypass delivery of verification email in
dev/test deployments (default: `false`). Verification/recovery policy
remains in coauth; soland only provides DID/webvh primitives.

password_change_allowed.description:
Allow users to change their password (default: `true`). Irrelevant when
password login is disabled.

password_recovery_enabled.description:
Permit email-based password recovery (default: `false`). Irrelevant when
password login is disabled.

account_deactivation_allowed.description: Allow users to deactivate (delete) their own account (default: `true`)

login_with_email_allowed.description:
Permit logging in via email address rather than username
(default: `false`). Irrelevant when password login is disabled.

admin_portal_url.description:
Optional URL of the external admin portal.

When set, users with administrative access will see a link to the
portal in the account UI.

registration_token_required.description:
Require a registration token for new password-based accounts
(default: `false`). Has no effect when registration is off.

bootstrap_admin_token.description:
Optional bootstrap token that allows one registration to claim the
first administrator role while no admin users exist.

ExperimentalConfig.description: Experimental feature flags -- change at your own risk

access_token_ttl.description:
Lifetime of access tokens (seconds). Default: 300 (5 min). Hard-capped
at 900 (15 min): bearer access tokens must be short-lived, matching the
`capped_bearer_expiry <= 15min` rule enforced on the soland side. The
issuance path additionally clamps to this ceiling as a defence in depth.

inactive_session_expiration.description: Opt-in automatic expiration of sessions that have been idle

plan_management_iframe_uri.description:
URI for an embeddable plan-management interface. Forwarded to the
client and injected into an `iframe src`, so it is validated at
config load time: it MUST parse as an absolute URL with an `https`
scheme. Non-`https` schemes (notably `javascript:` / `data:`) are
rejected to prevent script injection / phishing through the embed.

session_limit.description: Limit the total number of concurrent application sessions per user

InactiveSessionExpirationConfig.description: Tuning options for automatic expiration of idle sessions

ttl.description: Duration (in seconds) after which an idle session is terminated

expire_oauth_sessions.description: Apply the inactivity timeout to OAuth sessions

expire_user_sessions.description: Apply the inactivity timeout to browser (user) sessions

SessionLimitConfig.description: Hard and soft caps on the number of active sessions per user

StorageConfig.description:
Storage backend configuration.

Supports local filesystem or S3-compatible object storage.

```yaml
storage:
  backend: fs
  root: ./data/media
```

or:

```yaml
storage:
  backend: s3
  bucket: my-bucket
  region: us-east-1
  endpoint: https://account.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
```

oneOf.description: S3-compatible object storage (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, `MinIO`, etc.).

endpoint.description: S3 endpoint URL. Required for non-AWS services.

redirect.description: Redirect downloads to presigned S3 URLs.
